questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What is the name of the blood vessel that carries deoxygenated blood from the body to the heart in a frog?
questions.solution: Frog's heart is a muscular structure with three chambers. It receives deoxygenated blood from body parts through the major veins called vena cava. Vena cava carries deoxygenated blood. Aorta and pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood. Whereas, pulmonary artery will carry deoxygenated blood towards the lungs.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Choose the correct statements regarding frog's anatomy :
A. Hepatic portal system is the special venous connection between liver and intestine.
B. There are twelve pairs of cranial nerves arising from the brain.
C. The ureters and oviducts open separately into the cloaca in female frogs.
D. Hind-brain consists of cerebellum, medulla oblongata and optic lobes.
E. Sinus venosus joins the right atrium of heart.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Statement A is correct. The hepatic portal system is a special venous connection between the liver and the intestine in frogs.

Statement B is incorrect. There are ten pairs of cranial nerves arising from the brain in frogs, not twelve.

Statement C is correct. In female frogs, the ureters and oviducts open separately into the cloaca, whereas in male frogs, ureters act as urinogenital ducts.

Statement D is incorrect. The hind-brain consists of the cerebellum and medulla oblongata. The optic lobes are a part of the mid-brain.

Statement E is correct. The sinus venosus is a triangular structure that joins the right atrium of the heart and receives blood through the venae cavae.

Therefore, the correct statements are A, C, and E.

Answer: A, C and E only

Which of the following is/are present in female cockroach?
A. Collateral gland
B. Mushroom gland
C. Spermatheca
D. Anal style
E. Phallic gland

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option (4) as
A. Collateral gland Present in female cockroaches
It is a pair of gland that secrete the hard egg case or ootheca
B. Mushroom gland Absent in female cockroaches
Present in males in the $6^{\text{th }}$ to $7^{\text{th }}$ abdominal segments

Present in males and project backwardly from $9^{\text{th }}$ sternum

Present in males as a large club shaped gland located below the ejaculatory duct and reaches anteriorly up to the $5^{\text{th }}$ abdominal segment.

Whereas, structures indicated by ' $B$ ', ' $D$ ' and ' $E$ ' are present in males.

Option (3) is incorrect as it represents only a single structure which is present in female cockroaches.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In frogs, the number of pairs of cranial nerves arising from the brain are __________.
questions.solution:
In frogs, the nervous system is organized into a central nervous system, a peripheral nervous system, and an autonomic nervous system.

The peripheral nervous system consists of cranial nerves arising from the brain and spinal nerves arising from the spinal cord.

There are exactly $10$ pairs of cranial nerves present in frogs.

Answer: $10$

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is characteristics feature of cockroach regarding sexual dimorphism?
options: Dark brown body colour and anal cerci
questions.solution:
Cockroaches are dioecious and both sexes have well-developed reproductive organs. The male and female cockroaches can be easily distinguished based on the presence or absence of anal styles.

Males bear a pair of short, threadlike anal styles which are absent in females. In both sexes, the 10th segment bears a pair of jointed filamentous structures called anal cerci.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Tegmina in cockroach, arises from:
questions.solution:
Two pairs of wings, forewings, and hindwings are present on the dorsal side. Forewings are the first pair of dark, opaque, thick, leathery wings that are protective in function. Hindwings are thin, broad, membranous, delicate, and transparent. These are attached to the tergum of the metathorax. These are helpful in flight and hence are also called true wings

Tegmina is the forewing of cockroaches and is called mesothoracic due to its origin.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following statements is correct about the type of junction and their role in our body?
options: Adhering junctions facilitate the cells to communicate with each other.
Tight junctions help to stop substances from leaking across a tissue.
Tight junctions help to perform cementing to keep neighbouring cells together.
Gap junctions help to create gap between the cells and tissues.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option (2), because tight junctions help to stop substances from leaking across a tissue.
Options (1), (3) and (4) are incorrect because
- Adhering junctions perform cementing to keep neighbouring cells together.
- Gap junctions facilitate the cells to communicate with each other by connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells for rapid transfer of ions, small molecules and sometimes big molecules.

options: the cockroach does not have nervous system.
the head holds a small proportion of a nervous system while the rest is situated along the ventral part of its body.

questions.solution:
NERVOUS SYSTEM:

The nervous system of the cockroach consists of a series of fused, segmentally arranged ganglia joined by paired longitudinal connectives on the ventral side.

questions.q: Cuboidal epithelium with brush border of microvilli is found in
questions.solution:
SIMPLE CILIATED EPITHELIUM:

Structure: The simple ciliated epithelium comprises cells bearing fine, vibratile cilia on their free surface. Mixed with the ciliated cells, mucus-secreting goblet cells are found at intervals. It is of two types:

* Cuboidal ciliated epithelium: It comprises cuboidal cells bearing cilia on their free surface. It is found in the nephrons and facilitates urine formation.

* Columnar ciliated epithelium: It comprises columnar cells that bear cilia on the free surface. It forms the lining of the ventricles of the brain, oviducts, central canal of the spinal cord, nasal passages, and terminal bronchioles. It is also present in the lining of the alimentary canal.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The ciliated epithelial cells are required to move particles or mucus in a specific direction. In humans, these cells are mainly present in:
questions.solution:
The human tracheobronchial tree is lined by pseudostratified, ciliated epithelium from the larynx down to the level of the terminal bronchiole. The nasal cavity (apart from its most anterior portion) and the paranasal sinuses are also lined by ciliated epithelium.
The epithelium of the human fallopian tube is a mixture of ciliated and nonciliated cells. Scattered ciliated cells are also found in the endometrium. The function of these ciliated cells is generally believed to be the transport of eggs, zygotes, and secretions. The cilia may further help to maintain the patency of the oviductal lumen

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Select the correct sequence of organs in the alimentary canal of cockroach starting from mouth:
options: Pharynx $\to$ Oesophagus $\to$ Crop $\to$ Gizzard $\to$ Ileum $\to$ Colon $\to$ Rectum
Pharynx $\to$ Oesophagus $\to$ Gizzard $\to$ Crop $\to$ Ileum $\to$ Colon $\to$ Rectum
Pharynx $\to$ Oesophagus $\to$ Gizzard $\to$ Ileum $\to$ Crop $\to$ Colon $\to$ Rectum
Pharynx $\to$ Oesophagus $\to$ Ileum $\to$ Crop $\to$ Gizzard $\to$ Colon $\to$ Rectum
questions.solution:
Digestion begins at the mouth where the structures such as mandibles and maxillae help chew the food. The mouth open into a short tubular region called pharynx. The enzymes salivary carbohydrases digests food partially and the saliva juice lubricates the food to help swallow it, from where the bolus moves to the esophagus and then onto the crop. Here food remains in its masticated form temporarily. The food now moves to the gizzard where it’s grinding takes place. A valve named stomodeal is present right at the joint of gizzard and stomach.
This valve prevents the regurgitation of food while ensuring the smooth passage of food in the stomach. The food that has entered the stomach are treated by the digestive enzymes created by the gastric caeca. The enzymes involved are invertase, amylase, maltase, and lipase. The residual fats, proteins, and carbohydrates will be absorbed here.

So, the correct sequence is:

Pharynx $\to$ Oesophagus $\to$ Crop $\to$ Gizzard $\to$ Ileum $\to$ Colon $\to$ Rectum

questions.q: Which one of the following is one of the paths followed by air or $\mathrm{O}_2$ during respiration in the adult male Periplaneta americana as it enters the animal body?Spiracle in metathorax, trachea, tracheoles, oxygen diffuses into cells
options: Spiracle in metathorax, trachea, tracheoles, oxygen diffuses into cells
Mouth, bronchial tube, trachea, oxygen enters cells
Spiracles in prothorax, tracheoles, trachea, oxygen diffuses into cells.
questions.solution:
The trachea is a dense array of a network of air tubes found in the internal system. Tracheae are known to balance the pressure inside the system. When oxygenrich air enters into the body of the cockroach via spiracles into the tracheal tubes, it diffuses into various tissues and cells of the body. Here, oxygen is used up to liberate energy. Likewise, carbon-dioxide rich air passes into the trachea and moves to the outwards through the spiracles. Carbon dioxide is given out as a result of the respiratory process. (Ref. to Fig. 14.9)
Related Theory The exchange of gases depends on the metabolic rate and temperature. When air enters the tracheoles, oxygen diffuses faster into the tissues due to its high partial pressure. At the same time the carbon dioxide of tissues, instead of passing into the tracheal system, goes into the haemolymph. Carbon dioxide is carried more quickly into the haemolymph due to its greater solubility in it. This carbon dioxide accumulates near the spiracles and diffuses in to the atrial chambers near the spiracles and goes out in bursts through the abdominal spiracles.

options: Malpighian tubules convert nitrogenous wastes into urea.
Males bear short anal styles not present in females.
Nervous system comprises of a dorsal nerve cord and ten pairs of ganglia.

Veins are strongly chitinised and enclose $a$ small trachea; the larger veins also contain a fine nerve fibre.

questions.solution:

questions.solution:
Collagen is the most abundant protein in the animal world. This is one of the main components of our connective tissue and are associated with bones, cartilages, tendons, skin etc. It is the substance that holds the body together. Collagen forms a scaffold to provide strength and structure.

The frog excretes urea and thus is a ureotelic animal. It never becomes uricotelic.
In frog, fertilization is external and takes place in water.

questions.q: Which one of the following pair of items correctly belongs to the category of organs mentioned against it?
options:
Thorn of
- Analogous organs
Bougainvillea and tendrils of Cucurbita
Nictitating - Vestigial organs membrane and blind spot in human eye
Nephridia - Excretory organs of earthworm and Malpighian tubules of cockroach
Wings of honey bee - Homologous organs and wings of crow
questions.solution:
In annelids like Nereis, earthworm, leech etc the tubular coiled structures called nephridia are excretory organs. In phylum-Arthropoda, insects, centipedes, millipedes and arachnides possess Malpighian tubules as their principal excretory organ.
Analogous organs have almost similar appearance and perform the same function but develop in totally different groups and are totally different in their basic structure and developmental origin, eg, wings of butterfly, birds, bats.
The homologous organs have common origin, perform varied functions and have different appearance, eg, thorns of Bougainvillea and tendrils of Cucurbita.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Mast cells secrete:
questions.solution:
Mast cells are found in mucous membranes and connective tissues and are important for wound healing and defense against pathogens via the inflammatory response. The mast cell granules are composed of heparin and histamine. They secrete heparin, and histamine when they are activated due to toxic substance or pathogen. When released histamine cause blood vessels to dilate, increasing blood flow and cell trafficking to the area of infection. It is also involved in the inflammatory response. serotonin, a protein which acts as a vasoconstrictor to stop bleeding and to increase blood pressure is also released from mast cells.
Related Theory
As part of an immune response to foreign pathogens, histamine is produced by basophils and by mast cells found in nearby connective tissues. Histamine increases the permeability of the capillaries to white blood cells and some proteins, to allow them to engage pathogens in the infected tissues.

questions.q: In which one of the following preparations are you likely to come across cell junctions most frequently?
questions.solution:
Cell junctions are especially abundant in epithelial tissues. They consist of protein complexes and provide contact between neighbouring cells, between a cell and the extracellular matrix, or they built up the paracellular barrier of epithelia and control the paracellular transport. The other three (thrombocytes, tendon and hyaline cartilage) belongs to connective tissue. Thrombocytes or platelets aid the formation of blood clots by releasing various protein substances. Tendon attaches a muscle to a bone and hyaline cartilage gives flexibility and support at the joints.
Related Theory
Ciliated epithelium is a region of epithelium consisting of columnar or cuboidal cells bearing hairlike appendages that are capable of beating rapidly. It ofien occurs in the vicinity of mucus-secreting goblet cells.

questions.solution:
Explanation of the correct option:

Ligaments are the connective tissues that join bones to bones.
Option B:
Bones are joined with muscles with the help of tendons.
Option C:
Fat bodies are connected to muscles via adipose tissues.
Final answer: Areolar connective tissue joins integument with muscles.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Presence of gills in the tadpole of frog indicates that:
options: fishes were amphibious in the past
frogs will have gills in future
questions.solution:
Tadpoles are the larval forms of frog and toads. They respire through gills whereas the adult form respire through the skin and lungs. Since, fishes also respires through gills. Hence, presence of gills in the tadpole indicates that frogs are evolved from gilled ancestors.
Related Theory
"Ontogeny recapitulates phylogeny" mean that the development of individual organisms (ontogeny) follows (recapitulates) the same phases of the evolution of larger ancestral groups of related organisms (phylogeny).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In unicellular organisms, which cell functions are performed by a single cell?
questions.solution:
.

In the preceding chapters you came across a large variety of organisms, both unicellular and multicellular, of the animal kingdom. In unicellular organisms, all functions like digestion, respiration and reproduction are performed by a single cell. In the complex body of multicellular animals the same basic functions are carried out by different groups of cells in a well organised manner. The body of a simple organism like Hydra is made of different types of cells and the number of cells in each type can be in thousands. The human body is composed of billions of cells to perform various functions. How do these cells in the body work together? As you have already learnt in your earlier classes, in multicellular animals, a group of similar cells alongwith intercellular substances perform a specific function. Such an organisation is called tissue. You may be surprised to know that all complex animals consist of only four basic types of tissues. These tissues are organised in specific proportion and pattern to form an organ like stomach, lung, heart and kidney. When two or more organs perform a common function by their physical and/or chemical interaction, they together form organ system, e.g., digestive system, respiratory system, etc. Cells, tissues, organs and organ systems split up the work in a way that exhibits division of labour and contribute to the survival of the body as a whole.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What is essential for more efficient and better-coordinated activities of millions of cells?
options: Organization into organs and organ systems
questions.solution: The basic tissues as you have learnt in earlier classes, organise to form organs which in turn associate to form organ systems in the multicellular organisms. Such an organisation is essential for more efficient and better coordinated activities of millions of cells constituting an organism. Each organ in our body is made of one or more type of tissues. For example, our heart consists of all the four types of tissues, i.e., epithelial, connective, muscular and neural. We also notice, after some careful study that the complexity in organ and organ systems displays certain discernable trend. This discernable trend is called evolutionary trend (You will study the details in class XII). In this chapter, you are being introduced to morphology and anatomy of frog. Morphology refers to study of form or externally visible features. In the case of plants or microbes, the term morphology precisely means only this. In case of animals this refers to the external appearance of the organs or parts of the body. The word anatomy conventionally is used for the study of morphology of internal organs in the animals. You will learn the morphology and anatomy of frog representing vertebrates

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: To which class do frogs belong?
questions.solution:
Explanation

Frogs can live both on land and in freshwater and belong to class Amphibia of phylum Chordata. The most common species of frog found in India is Rana tigrina. They do not have constant body temperature i.e., their body temperature varies with the temperature of the environment. Such animals are called cold blooded or poikilotherms. You might have also noticed changes in the colour of the frogs while they are in grasses and on dry land. They have the ability to change the colour to hide them from their enemies (camouflage). This protective coloration is called mimicry. You may also know that frogs are not seen during peak summer and winter. During this period they take shelter in deep burrows to protect them from extreme heat and cold. This is known as summer sleep (aestivation) and winter sleep (hibernation) respectively.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What makes the skin of a frog smooth and slippery?
questions.solution: Have you ever touched the skin of frog? The skin is smooth and slippery due to the presence of mucus. The skin is always maintained in a moist condition. The colour of dorsal side of body is generally olive green with dark irregular spots. On the ventral side the skin is uniformly pale yellow. The frog never drinks water but absorb it through the skin. Body of a frog is divisible into head and trunk A neck and tail are absent. Above the mouth, a pair of nostrils is present. Eyes are bulged and covered by a nictitating membrane that protects them while in water. On either side of eyes a membranous tympanum (ear) receives sound signals. The forelimbs and hind limbs help in swimming, walking, leaping and burrowing. The hind limbs end in five digits and they are larger and muscular than fore limbs that end in four digits. Feet have webbed digits that help in swimming. Frogs exhibit sexual dimorphism. Male frogs can be distinguished by the presence of sound producing vocal sacs and also a copulatory pad on the first digit of the fore limbs which are absent in female frogs.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Why is the alimentary canal of frogs short?
questions.solution: The body cavity of frogs accommodate different organ systems such as digestive, circulatory, respiratory, nervous, excretory and reproductive systems with well developed structures and functions The digestive system consists of alimentary canal and digestive glands. The alimentary canal is short because frogs are carnivores and hence the length of intestine is reduced. The mouth opens into the buccal cavity that leads to the oesophagus through pharynx. Oesophagus is a short tube that opens into the stomach which in turn continues as the intestine, rectum and finally opens outside by the cloaca. Liver secretes bile that is stored in the gall bladder. Pancreas, a digestive gland produces pancreatic juice

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What captures food in frogs?
questions.solution: Food is captured by the bilobed tongue. Digestion of food takes place by the action of HCl and gastric juices secreted from the walls of the stomach. Partially digested food called chyme is passed from stomach to the first part of the small intestine, the duodenum. The duodenum receives bile from gall bladder and pancreatic juices from the pancreas through a common bile duct. Bile emulsifies fat and pancreatic juices digest carbohydrates and proteins. Final digestion takes place in the intestine. Digested food is absorbed by the numerous finger-like folds in the inner wall of intestine called villi and microvilli. The undigested solid waste moves into the rectum and passes out through cloaca.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: How do frogs respire in water?
questions.solution: Frogs respire on land and in the water by two different methods. In water, skin acts as aquatic respiratory organ (cutaneous respiration). Dissolved oxygen in the water is exchanged through the skin by diffusion. On land, the buccal cavity, skin and lungs act as the respiratory organs. The respiration by lungs is called pulmonary respiration. The lungs are a pair of elongated, pink coloured sac-like structures present in the upper part of the trunk region (thorax). Air enters through the nostrils into the buccal cavity and then to lungs. During aestivation and hibernation gaseous exchange takes place through skin.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What type of vascular system do frogs have?
questions.solution: The vascular system of frog is well-developed closed type. Frogs have a lymphatic system also. The blood vascular system involves heart, blood vessels and blood. The lymphatic system consists of lymph, lymph channels and lymph nodes. Heart is a muscular structure situated in the upper part of the body cavity. It has three chambers, two atria and one ventricle and is covered by a membrane called pericardium. A triangular structure called sinus venosus joins the right atrium. It receives blood through the major veins called vena cava. The ventricle opens into a sac- like conus arteriosus on the ventral side of the heart. The blood from the heart is carried to all parts of the body by the arteries (arterial system). The veins collect blood from different parts of body to the heart and form the venous system. Special venous connection between liver and intestine as well as the kidney and lower parts of the body are present in frogs. The former is called hepatic portal system and the latter is called renal portal system. The blood is composed of plasma and cells. The blood cells are RBC (red blood cells) or erythrocytes, WBC (white blood cells) or leucocytes and platelets. RBC’s are nucleated and contain red coloured pigment namely haemoglobin. The lymph is different from blood. It lacks few proteins and RBCs. The blood carries nutrients, gases and water to the respective sites during the circulation. The circulation of blood is achieved by the pumping action of the muscular heart.

questions.solution: <mark>The elimination of nitrogenous wastes is carried out by a well developed excretory system.</mark>The elimination of nitrogenous wastes is carried out by a well developed excretory system. The excretory system consists of a pair of kidneys, ureters, cloaca and urinary bladder. These are compact, dark red and bean like structures situated a little posteriorly in the body cavity on both sides of vertebral column. Each kidney is composed of several structural and functional units called uriniferous tubules or nephrons. Two ureters emerge from the kidneys in the male frogs. The ureters act as urinogenital duct which opens into the cloaca. In females the ureters and oviduct open seperately in the cloaca. The thin-walled urinary bladder is present ventral to the rectum which also opens in the cloaca. The frog excretes urea and thus is a ureotelic animal. Excretory wastes are carried by blood into the kidney where it is separated and excreted.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What does the control and coordination system in frogs include?
options: Both neural system and endocrine glands
questions.solution: The system for control and coordination is highly evolved in the frog. It includes both neural system and endocrine glands. The chemical coordination of various organs of the body is achieved by hormones which are secreted by the endocrine glands. The prominent endocrine glands found in frog are pituitary, thyroid, parathyroid, thymus, pineal body, pancreatic islets, adrenals and gonads. The nervous system is organised into a central nervous system (brain and spinal cord), a peripheral nervous system (cranial and spinal nerves) and an autonomic nervous system (sympathetic and parasympathetic). There are ten pairs of cranial nerves arising from the brain. Brain is enclosed in a bony structure called brain box (cranium). The brain is divided into fore-brain, mid-brain and hind-brain. Forebrain includes olfactory lobes, paired cerebral hemispheres and unpaired diencephalon. The midbrain is characterised by a pair of optic lobes. Hind-brain consists of cerebellum and medulla oblongata. The medulla oblongata passes out through the foramen magnum and continues into spinal cord, which is enclosed in the vertebral column.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which sense organ in frogs is responsible for touch?
questions.solution: Frog has different types of sense organs, namely organs of touch (sensory papillae), taste (taste buds), smell (nasal epithelium), vision (eyes) and hearing (tympanum with internal ears). Out of these, eyes and internal ears are well-organised structures and the rest are cellular aggregations around nerve endings. Eyes in a frog are a pair of spherical structures situated in the orbit in skull. These are simple eyes (possessing only one unit). External ear is absent in frogs and only tympanum can be seen externally. The ear is an organ of hearing as well as balancing (equilibrium).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What are the male reproductive organs in frogs?
options: A pair of yellowish ovoid testes
questions.solution: Frogs have well organised male and female reproductive systems. Male reproductive organs consist of a pair of yellowish ovoid testes , which are found adhered to the upper part of kidneys by a double fold of peritoneum called mesorchium. Vasa efferentia are 10-12 in number that arise from testes. They enter the kidneys on their side and open into Bidder’s canal. Finally it communicates with the urinogenital duct that comes out of the kidneys and opens into the cloaca. The cloaca is a small, median chamber that is used to pass faecal matter, urine and sperms to the exterior. The female reproductive organs include a pair of ovaries The ovaries are situated near kidneys and there is no functional connection with kidneys. A pair of oviduct arising from the ovaries opens into the cloaca separately. A mature female can lay 2500 to 3000 ova at a time. Fertilisation is external and takes place in water. Development involves a larval stage called tadpole. Tadpole undergoes metamorphosis to form the adult.Frogs are beneficial for mankind because they eat insects and protect the crop. Frogs maintain ecological balance because these serve as an important link of food chain and food web in the ecosystem. In some countries the muscular legs of frog are used as food by man.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The stomach of the frog contains
questions.solution: Food is captured by the bilobed tongue. Digestion of food takes place by the action of HCl and gastric juices secreted from the walls of the stomach. Partially digested food called chyme is passed from the stomach to the first part of the intestine, the duodenum. The duodenum receives bile from gallbladder and pancreatic juices from the pancreas through a common bile duct. Bile emulsifies fat and pancreatic juices digest carbohydrates and proteins. Final digestion takes place in the intestine. Digested food is absorbed by the numerous finger-like folds in the inner wall of intestine called villi and microvilli. The undigested solid waste moves into the rectum and passes out through cloaca.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Open into cloaca of a female frog (I) 2 oviducts (II) 2 ureters (III) 2 urinogenital ducts (IV) Alimentary canal (V) Bidder canal
questions.solution: The elimination of nitrogenous wastes is carried out by a well developed excretory system. The excretory system consists of a pair of kidneys, ureters, cloaca and urinary bladder. These are compact, dark red and bean like structures situated a little posteriorly in the body cavity on both sides of the vertebral column. Each kidney is composed of several structural and functional units called uriniferous tubules of nephrons. Two ureters emerge from the kidneys in the male frogs. The ureters act as urinogenital ducts which open into the cloaca.   The ovaries are situated near kidneys and there is no functional connection with kidneys. A pair of oviducts arising from the ovaries opens into the cloaca separately. A mature female can lay 2500 to 3000 ova at a time. Fertilisation is external and takes place in water. Development involves a larval stage called tadpole. Tadpole undergoes metamorphosis to form the adult.   The digestive system consists of alimentary canal and digestive glands. The alimentary canal is short because frogs are carnivores and hence the length of intestine is reduced. The mouth opens into the buccal cavity that leads to the oesophagus through pharynx. Oesophagus is a short tube that opens into the stomach which in turn continues as the intestine, rectum and finally opens outside by the cloaca. Liver secretes bile that is stored in the gallbladder. Pancreas, a digestive gland, produces pancreatic juice.

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Cockroach is a uricotelic animal.
Reason (R): In cockroach, Malpighian tubules absorb nitrogenous wastes from haemolymph and convert them into uric acid, which is excreted out through the hindgut.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

Assertion is correct but Reason is not correct.
Assertion is not correct but Reason is correct.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct because cockroaches excrete uric acid as their primary nitrogenous waste, making them uricotelic.

Reason (R) is also correct and provides the exact physiological mechanism for the assertion. The Malpighian tubules, which are the primary excretory organs in cockroaches, absorb nitrogenous waste products from the haemolymph and convert them into uric acid. This uric acid is then eliminated through the hindgut.

Therefore, both Assertion and Reason are correct, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding epithelial tissues:
(A) Simple squamous epithelium is found in the walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs.
(B) The epithelium of the proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) of the nephron in the kidney has microvilli.
(C) Ciliated epithelium is found in the inner lining of the ducts of salivary glands.
(D) Goblet cells of the alimentary canal are examples of unicellular glands.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is correct as simple squamous epithelium forms a diffusion boundary and is found in the walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs.

Statement (B) is correct because the cuboidal epithelium of the proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) of the nephron has microvilli to increase the surface area for absorption.

Statement (C) is incorrect because the inner lining of the ducts of salivary glands is lined by compound epithelium, not ciliated epithelium. Ciliated epithelium is found in hollow organs like bronchioles and fallopian tubes.

Statement (D) is correct as goblet cells of the alimentary canal are isolated glandular cells, which are examples of unicellular glands.

Therefore, exactly three statements are correct.

Answer: Three

Reason (R): Blood is a fluid connective tissue containing plasma, red blood cells (RBC), white blood cells (WBC) and platelets.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true as in all connective tissues except blood, the cells (like fibroblasts) secrete fibres of structural proteins called collagen or elastin.

Reason (R) is also true as blood is a fluid connective tissue containing plasma, red blood cells (RBC), white blood cells (WBC) and platelets.

However, Reason (R) does not explain Assertion (A). The reason blood does not secrete fibres is due to the absence of fibre-secreting cells (fibroblasts), not merely because it contains plasma and blood components. Therefore, both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

Assertion (A): In frogs, venous blood from the hindlimbs does not drain directly into the main systemic veins leading to the heart.
Reason (R): Frogs possess a renal portal system that first routes blood from the lower body parts to the kidneys.

(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
In frogs, special venous connections are present between the lower parts of the body and the kidneys, known as the renal portal system.

Due to this system, venous blood from the hindlimbs and lower body parts is first routed to the kidneys before it eventually reaches the heart. Therefore, the blood does not drain directly into the main systemic veins leading to the heart.

Thus, both Assertion and Reason are correct, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

Option 2 correctly pairs the male external copulatory pad on the forelimbs with the male internal urinogenital duct.

questions.q:
Read the following anatomical locations carefully:
(i) Dry surface of the skin
(ii) Moist surface of buccal cavity
(iii) Inner lining of ducts of salivary glands
(iv) Inner lining of pancreatic ducts
(v) Proximal convoluted tubule (PCT)
(vi) Inner surface of bronchioles

How many of the above locations are lined by compound epithelium?
questions.solution:
Compound epithelium is made of more than one layer of cells and has a limited role in secretion and absorption. Its main function is to provide protection against chemical and mechanical stresses.

According to NCERT, compound epithelium covers the dry surface of the skin, the moist surface of buccal cavity, pharynx, inner lining of ducts of salivary glands and of pancreatic ducts. Thus, locations (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv) are lined by compound epithelium.

The proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) of the nephron in the kidney is lined by simple cuboidal epithelium (with brush border). The inner surface of hollow organs like bronchioles is lined by ciliated epithelium.

Therefore, exactly four of the given locations are lined by compound epithelium.

Answer: Four

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following correctly identifies the epithelial tissue found in the inner lining of the stomach and intestine, along with its defining morphological characteristic?
options: Simple columnar epithelium; composed of a single layer of tall and slender cells with their nuclei located at the base
Simple columnar epithelium; composed of a single layer of tall and slender cells with centrally located nuclei
Simple cuboidal epithelium; composed of a single layer of cube-like cells with their nuclei located at the base
Compound epithelium; composed of multiple layers of cells with a limited role in secretion
questions.solution:
The inner lining of the stomach and intestine is composed of simple columnar epithelium, which helps in secretion and absorption.

According to NCERT, simple columnar epithelium is composed of a single layer of tall and slender cells, and their nuclei are characteristically located at the base, making the first option correct.

The second option is incorrect because the nuclei in columnar cells are basal, not central. The third option is incorrect as simple cuboidal epithelium is typically found in ducts of glands and tubular parts of nephrons, not the stomach lining. The fourth option is incorrect because compound epithelium is multi-layered and covers surfaces subjected to mechanical or chemical stress (like the buccal cavity or pharynx), whereas the stomach and intestine require a single-layered epithelium for efficient secretion and absorption.

Answer: Simple columnar epithelium; composed of a single layer of tall and slender cells with their nuclei located at the base

Read the following statements regarding glandular epithelium:

Statement I: Some columnar or cuboidal cells get specialised for secretion to form glandular epithelium.
Statement II: Goblet cells are examples of multicellular glands found in the alimentary canal.
Statement III: Exocrine glands secrete mucus, saliva, earwax, oil, milk, and digestive enzymes through ducts.
Statement IV: Endocrine glands are ductless and their products are called hormones.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement I is correct. Glandular epithelium is formed when some columnar or cuboidal cells get specialised for secretion.

Statement II is incorrect. Goblet cells of the alimentary canal consist of isolated glandular cells and are examples of unicellular glands, not multicellular glands. Salivary glands are examples of multicellular glands.

Statement III is correct. Exocrine glands release their secretory products like mucus, saliva, earwax, oil, milk, and digestive enzymes through ducts or tubes.

Statement IV is correct. Endocrine glands lack ducts and secrete their products, known as hormones, directly into the fluid bathing the gland.

Thus, exactly three statements (I, III, and IV) are correct.

Answer: Three

questions.q:
A microscopic examination of a connective tissue reveals a hard and non-pliable ground substance that is rich in calcium salts and collagen fibres.

Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding the tissue described above?
options: Its cells are called osteocytes and are present in spaces called lacunae.
It interacts with skeletal muscles attached to them to bring about movements.
It is classified as a dense regular connective tissue.
The bone marrow in some of them is the site of production of blood cells.
questions.solution:
The tissue described has a hard and non-pliable ground substance rich in calcium salts and collagen fibres, which is the characteristic feature of bone.

Bones are classified as specialised connective tissues, not dense regular connective tissues. Dense regular connective tissues include tendons and ligaments.

The other statements are correct for bone: bone cells (osteocytes) are present in spaces called lacunae; bones interact with skeletal muscles to bring about movements; and bone marrow in some bones is the site of production of blood cells (hemopoiesis).

Answer: It is classified as a dense regular connective tissue.

questions.q: Read the following statements regarding the thorax and appendages of a cockroach and choose the incorrect statement.
options: The thorax consists of three distinct segments: prothorax, mesothorax, and metathorax.
Each of the three thoracic segments bears a pair of walking legs.
The hindwings arise from the metathorax, are transparent and membranous, and are used in flight.

questions.solution:
The thorax of a cockroach consists of three parts: prothorax, mesothorax, and metathorax. Each of these segments bears a pair of walking legs.

Cockroaches have two pairs of wings. The first pair of wings arises from the mesothorax, not the prothorax. These forewings are called tegmina and are opaque, dark, and leathery. They cover the hindwings when at rest.

The second pair of wings arises from the metathorax. These hindwings are transparent, membranous, and are used in flight.

Thus, the statement claiming that tegmina arise from the prothorax is incorrect.

Answer: The first pair of wings, known as tegmina, arises from the prothorax and is opaque, dark, and leathery.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In a cockroach, the primary excretory tubules absorb nitrogenous waste products from the haemolymph and convert them into uric acid. Which specific types of cells line these tubules?
questions.solution:
In cockroaches, excretion is performed by Malpighian tubules. According to NCERT, each Malpighian tubule is lined by glandular and ciliated cells.

These cells absorb nitrogenous waste products from the haemolymph and convert them into uric acid, which is then excreted out through the hindgut. Simple squamous epithelium is found in structures like the Bowman's capsule of humans, while brush-bordered cuboidal cells line the proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) of human nephrons.

Answer: Glandular and ciliated cells

Assertion (A): In cockroach, the gizzard acts as an efficient grinding mill for food particles.
Reason (R): The gizzard has an outer layer of thick circular muscles and a thick inner cuticle forming six highly chitinous plates called teeth.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
In the alimentary canal of a cockroach, the crop is followed by the gizzard or proventriculus. The gizzard helps in grinding the food particles, making the Assertion true.

This grinding action is structurally supported by its anatomy: it possesses an outer layer of thick circular muscles and a thick inner cuticle that forms six highly chitinous plates known as teeth. This makes the Reason true.

Because the structural features described in the Reason directly enable the grinding function stated in the Assertion, the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements carefully:

(A) Some squamous or cuboidal cells get specialised for secretion to form glandular epithelium.
(B) Goblet cells of the alimentary canal are examples of isolated glandular cells.
(C) Exocrine glands secrete their products directly into the fluid bathing the gland.
(D) Saliva, earwax and milk are secretions of exocrine glands.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Let us evaluate each statement based on the NCERT description of glandular epithelium:

Statement (A) is incorrect. It is some of the columnar or cuboidal cells (not squamous) that get specialised for secretion and are called glandular epithelium.

Statement (B) is correct. Unicellular glands consist of isolated glandular cells, and goblet cells of the alimentary canal are the classic example.

Statement (C) is incorrect. Exocrine glands release their products through ducts or tubes. It is the endocrine glands (which lack ducts) that secrete their products (hormones) directly into the fluid bathing the gland.

Statement (D) is correct. Exocrine glands secrete mucus, saliva, earwax, oil, milk, digestive enzymes, and other cell products.

Since statements (B) and (D) are correct, exactly two statements are correct.

Answer: Two

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A student observes a cockroach specimen and notes that its 7th sternum is boat-shaped and, together with the 8th and 9th sterna, forms a brood or genital pouch. Which of the following structures will be absent in this specimen?
questions.solution:
The presence of a boat-shaped 7th sternum that forms a genital pouch along with the 8th and 9th sterna is a characteristic feature of a female cockroach.

Female cockroaches possess anal cerci, collateral glands, and spermathecal pores as part of their anatomy. However, they lack anal styles, which are short, thread-like structures found exclusively in male cockroaches.

Answer: Anal styles

questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding the nervous system of a frog is incorrect?
options: The peripheral nervous system consists of cranial and spinal nerves.
Twelve pairs of cranial nerves arise from the brain.
The autonomic nervous system consists of sympathetic and parasympathetic chains.
The medulla oblongata passes out through the foramen magnum and continues into the spinal cord.
questions.solution:
In frogs, exactly $10$ pairs of cranial nerves arise from the brain, not $12$ pairs. Humans and other mammals have $12$ pairs of cranial nerves, which is a common point of confusion.

The other statements are factually correct according to NCERT: the peripheral nervous system is indeed made up of cranial and spinal nerves; the autonomic nervous system consists of sympathetic and parasympathetic chains; and the medulla oblongata exits the skull through the foramen magnum to continue as the spinal cord.

Answer: Twelve pairs of cranial nerves arise from the brain.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the structures associated with the alimentary canal of a cockroach:

List-IList-II
(A) Crop(I) Grinding of food particles
(B) Gizzard(II) Secreting digestive juice
(C) Hepatic caeca(III) Storing of food
(D) Malpighian tubules(IV) Removal of excretory products

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
In the alimentary canal of a cockroach, the crop is a sac-like structure used for storing food. The gizzard (proventriculus) has an outer layer of thick circular muscles and thick inner cuticle forming six highly chitinous plates called teeth, which help in the grinding of food particles. A ring of 6-8 blind tubules called hepatic or gastric caeca is present at the junction of foregut and midgut, which secrete digestive juice. At the junction of midgut and hindgut is another ring of 100-150 yellow-coloured thin filamentous Malpighian tubules, which help in the removal of excretory products from haemolymph.

Therefore, the correct match is (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(IV).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(IV)

(A) In dense regular tissue, collagen fibres are present in rows between many parallel bundles of fibres.
(B) Ligaments attach skeletal muscles to bones and are dense regular tissues.

(D) Cartilage is a specialised connective tissue with a solid and pliable intercellular material.

questions.solution:
Statement (A) is correct as dense regular connective tissues have collagen fibres present in rows between many parallel bundles of fibres.

Statement (B) is incorrect because ligaments attach one bone to another, whereas tendons attach skeletal muscles to bones. Both are dense regular connective tissues.

Statement (C) is correct as skin contains dense irregular connective tissue with differently oriented fibres.

Statement (D) is correct because cartilage is a specialised connective tissue whose intercellular material is solid and pliable.

Thus, exactly three statements are correct.

Answer: Three

Assertion (A): The main function of compound epithelium is to provide protection against chemical and mechanical stresses.
Reason (R): Compound epithelium is a multi-layered tissue that plays a major role in secretion and absorption.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true because compound epithelium is designed to protect underlying tissues against chemical and mechanical stresses, which is its primary function.

Reason (R) is false. While compound epithelium is indeed multi-layered, this structural feature means it has a very limited role in secretion and absorption. Tissues that play a major role in secretion and absorption are typically single-layered (simple epithelium).

Thus, (A) is true but (R) is false.

Answer: (A) is true but (R) is false

questions.subject: Zoology

options: They are a ring of 6-8 blind tubules present at the junction of the midgut and hindgut that secrete digestive juice.
They are a ring of 100-150 yellow-coloured thin filamentous tubules present at the junction of the midgut and hindgut that help in excretion.

They are a ring of 100-150 yellow-coloured thin filamentous tubules present at the junction of the midgut and hindgut that secrete digestive juice.
questions.solution:
In a cockroach, Malpighian tubules are the principal excretory organs. They are a ring of 100-150 yellow-coloured, thin filamentous tubules present at the junction of the midgut and hindgut. They help in the removal of excretory products from the haemolymph.

Therefore, statements placing Malpighian tubules at the foregut-midgut junction, assigning them a digestive function, or confusing their count with that of hepatic caeca, are incorrect.

Answer: They are a ring of 100-150 yellow-coloured thin filamentous tubules present at the junction of the midgut and hindgut that help in excretion.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements carefully:

A. All cells in epithelium are held together with abundant intercellular material.
B. Tight junctions perform cementing to keep neighbouring cells together.
C. Gap junctions facilitate communication by connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells.
D. Specialised junctions provide only functional links between individual cells in animal tissues.

How many of the given statements are incorrect?
questions.solution:
Statement A is incorrect because all cells in epithelium are held together with little (not abundant) intercellular material.

Statement B is incorrect because adhering junctions (not tight junctions) perform cementing to keep neighbouring cells together. Tight junctions stop substances from leaking across a tissue.

Statement C is correct as gap junctions facilitate cell communication by connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells.

Statement D is incorrect because specialised junctions provide both structural and functional links between individual cells in animal tissues, not just functional links.

Therefore, three statements (A, B, and D) are incorrect.

Answer: Three

Statement (D) is incorrect: Uric acid is excreted out through the hindgut, not the midgut.

Thus, exactly two statements ((A) and (C)) are correct.

Answer: Two

questions.q:
While observing the epithelial lining of the alimentary canal, a student notes the presence of isolated secretory cells interspersed among the regular epithelial cells.

Identify these cells and their correct glandular classification.
options: Salivary glands, which act as multicellular exocrine glands
Goblet cells, which act as unicellular endocrine glands
Goblet cells, which act as multicellular exocrine glands
Goblet cells, which act as unicellular exocrine glands
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, some of the columnar or cuboidal cells get specialised for secretion and are called glandular epithelium. They are mainly of two types: unicellular, consisting of isolated glandular cells (e.g., goblet cells of the alimentary canal), and multicellular, consisting of clusters of cells (e.g., salivary glands).

Goblet cells secrete mucus, which is released through ducts or tubes, making them exocrine glands. Endocrine glands, on the other hand, are ductless and secrete hormones.

Therefore, the isolated secretory cells in the alimentary canal are goblet cells, and they function as unicellular exocrine glands.

Answer: Goblet cells, which act as unicellular exocrine glands

questions.solution:
Squamous epithelium is made of a single thin layer of flattened cells with irregular boundaries and is found in the walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs.

Cuboidal epithelium is composed of a single layer of cube-like cells and is commonly found in ducts of glands and tubular parts of nephrons in kidneys.

Columnar epithelium is composed of a single layer of tall and slender cells and is found in the lining of stomach and intestine.

Ciliated epithelium consists of columnar or cuboidal cells bearing cilia and is mainly present in the inner surface of hollow organs like bronchioles and fallopian tubes.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)

questions.q: Which of the following specialised junctions performs the function of cementing to keep neighbouring cells together in animal tissues?
questions.solution:
In animal tissues, adhering junctions perform cementing to keep neighbouring cells together.

Tight junctions help to stop substances from leaking across a tissue.

Gap junctions facilitate the cells to communicate with each other by connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells.

Plasmodesmata are cytoplasmic connections found in plant cells, not animal tissues.

Answer: Adhering junctions

options: Opaque, dark and leathery wings called tegmina
Transparent, membranous wings used in flight
Leathery, dark wings that are primarily used in flight
questions.solution:
In a cockroach, the first pair of wings arises from the mesothorax and is known as forewings or tegmina.

Tegmina are opaque, dark, and leathery. They cover the hindwings when at rest and are not used in flight.

The hindwings arise from the metathorax and are transparent, membranous, and used in flight. Halteres are reduced hindwings found in dipterans (like mosquitoes and houseflies), not in cockroaches.

Answer: Opaque, dark and leathery wings called tegmina

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In the alimentary canal of a cockroach, as a food bolus travels strictly through the foregut starting from the oesophagus, which of the following correctly represents the chronological sequence of primary functions it encounters?
questions.solution:
In the foregut of a cockroach, the oesophagus is a short tubular structure that primarily serves for the passage of food. It opens into a sac-like structure called the crop, which is used for the temporary storage of food. The crop is followed by the gizzard (proventriculus), which has an outer layer of thick circular muscles and a thick inner cuticle forming six highly chitinous plates called teeth. These teeth are used for the mechanical grinding of food particles.

Therefore, the correct functional sequence is Passage $\rightarrow$ Storage $\rightarrow$ Grinding. Enzymatic digestion primarily occurs in the midgut with the help of secretions from the hepatic caeca, not strictly within the foregut structures mentioned.

Answer: Passage $\rightarrow$ Storage $\rightarrow$ Grinding

Sound producing vocal sacs and a copulatory pad on the first digit of the forelimb

questions.solution:
In frogs, sexual dimorphism is clearly visible externally. Male frogs can be distinguished from female frogs by the presence of sound-producing vocal sacs and a copulatory pad on the first digit of the forelimbs. Both of these structures are absent in female frogs.

Tympanum, webbed feet, and nictitating membranes are morphological features present in both male and female frogs. The copulatory pad is specifically located on the forelimb, not the hind limb.

Answer: Sound producing vocal sacs and a copulatory pad on the first digit of the forelimb

questions.solution:

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In the body cavity of a cockroach, three major organ systems are represented by the heart, the alimentary canal, and the nerve cord. Which of the following represents the correct sequence of these structures from the dorsal side to the ventral side?
questions.solution:
In non-chordates like the cockroach, the circulatory system is dorsal, while the nervous system is ventral.

The heart of a cockroach consists of an elongated muscular tube lying along the mid-dorsal line of the thorax and abdomen. Therefore, it is the most dorsal structure among the three.

The alimentary canal runs centrally through the body cavity.

The nervous system consists of a double ventral nerve cord. Therefore, it is the most ventral structure.

The correct sequence from dorsal to ventral is Heart $\rightarrow$ Alimentary canal $\rightarrow$ Nerve cord.

Answer: Heart $\rightarrow$ Alimentary canal $\rightarrow$ Nerve cord

Read the following statement regarding the excretory system of a cockroach and choose the option that correctly fills the blanks A, B, C, and D.

In cockroach, excretion is primarily performed by __A__ which are present at the junction of __B__ and __C__, making the insect __D__.
options: A - Hepatic caeca, B - foregut, C - midgut, D - ammonotelic
A - Malpighian tubules, B - foregut, C - midgut, D - ureotelic
A - Malpighian tubules, B - midgut, C - hindgut, D - uricotelic
A - Malpighian tubules, B - midgut, C - hindgut, D - ureotelic
questions.solution:
In cockroaches, the primary excretory organs are the Malpighian tubules (A).

These are a ring of 100-150 yellow-coloured, thin filamentous structures located at the junction of the midgut (B) and hindgut (C).

The Malpighian tubules absorb nitrogenous waste from the haemolymph and convert it into uric acid, which is excreted out through the hindgut. Because it excretes uric acid, the cockroach is a uricotelic (D) insect.

Hepatic caeca are present at the junction of the foregut and midgut and are involved in secreting digestive juices, not excretion.

Answer: A - Malpighian tubules, B - midgut, C - hindgut, D - uricotelic

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements carefully:
(A) Fibres provide strength, elasticity and flexibility to the connective tissue.
(B) In all connective tissues except blood, the cells secrete fibres of structural proteins called collagen or elastin.
(C) Macrophages secrete modified polysaccharides, which accumulate between cells and fibres and act as matrix.
(D) Adipose tissue is a type of dense connective tissue located mainly beneath the skin.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is correct. The fibres of structural proteins (collagen or elastin) provide strength, elasticity and flexibility to the tissue.

Statement (B) is correct. Blood is the only connective tissue where cells do not secrete fibres.

Statement (C) is incorrect. The cells that secrete fibres (such as fibroblasts) also secrete modified polysaccharides which act as the matrix (ground substance). Macrophages are primarily phagocytic cells, not the primary matrix-secreting cells.

Statement (D) is incorrect. Adipose tissue is a type of loose connective tissue, not dense connective tissue.

Therefore, exactly two statements ((A) and (B)) are correct.

Answer: Two

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements carefully:
(I) Cells of cartilage (chondrocytes) are enclosed in small cavities within a solid and pliable matrix.
(II) Bone has a hard and non-pliable ground substance rich in calcium salts and collagen fibres.
(III) Areolar connective tissue contains fibroblasts, macrophages and mast cells.
(IV) Dense irregular connective tissue has fibroblasts and many fibres that are oriented parallel to each other.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (I) is correct as the intercellular material of cartilage is solid and pliable and resists compression. Cells of this tissue (chondrocytes) are enclosed in small cavities within the matrix secreted by them.

Statement (II) is correct as bone has a hard and non-pliable ground substance rich in calcium salts and collagen fibres which give bone its strength.

Statement (III) is correct as areolar tissue is a loose connective tissue that contains fibroblasts (cells that produce and secrete fibres), macrophages and mast cells.

Statement (IV) is incorrect because dense irregular connective tissue has fibroblasts and many fibres (mostly collagen) that are oriented differently, not parallel to each other. It is dense regular connective tissue that has collagen fibres present in rows between many parallel bundles of fibres.

Therefore, exactly three statements are correct.

Answer: Three

options: Tubular parts of nephrons in kidneys
Inner lining of stomach and intestine
questions.solution:
The given description corresponds to simple squamous epithelium, which is composed of a single thin layer of flattened cells with irregular boundaries and functions in forming a diffusion boundary.

Simple squamous epithelium is found in the walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs (alveoli).

questions.q: In all connective tissues, the cells secrete fibres of structural proteins called collagen or elastin, which provide strength, elasticity, and flexibility to the tissue. Identify the connective tissue which is an exception to this rule.
questions.solution:
According to the NCERT, in all connective tissues except blood, the cells secrete fibres of structural proteins called collagen or elastin.

Blood is a fluid connective tissue containing plasma, red blood cells (RBC), white blood cells (WBC) and platelets, and it lacks fibre-secreting cells (fibroblasts).

Cartilage, bone, and areolar tissue all contain cells that secrete structural fibres.

Answer: Blood

In a cockroach, the brain is represented by the supra-oesophageal ganglion, which is located in the head. According to NCERT, this ganglion specifically supplies nerves to the antennae and compound eyes. Therefore, removing the head severs the direct nerve supply to these sensory structures.

questions.solution:

Therefore, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) provides the correct functional explanation for the anatomical term used in Assertion (A).

questions.solution:
In frogs, there are two special venous connections called portal systems.

The hepatic portal system connects the intestine to the liver, meaning venous blood from the intestine first passes through the liver.

The renal portal system connects the lower parts of the body to the kidneys, meaning venous blood from the hindlimbs first passes through the kidneys.

Therefore, the intermediate organs are the liver and the kidney, respectively.

Answer: Liver and Kidney

options: Gap junctions in this tissue primarily help to stop substances from leaking across the tissue.
The cells constituting this tissue are modified columnar or cuboidal cells.
Its main function is to move particles or mucus in a specific direction over the epithelium.
Adhering junctions in this tissue perform cementing to keep neighbouring cells together.
questions.solution:
The tissue present in the inner surface of hollow organs like bronchioles and fallopian tubes is ciliated epithelium.

Ciliated epithelium consists of modified columnar or cuboidal cells that bear cilia on their free surface. Their main function is to move particles or mucus in a specific direction over the epithelium.

In epithelial tissues, tight junctions help to stop substances from leaking across a tissue, whereas gap junctions facilitate communication between cells by connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells. Therefore, the statement claiming that gap junctions prevent leakage is incorrect.

Answer: Gap junctions in this tissue primarily help to stop substances from leaking across the tissue.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Identify the correct sequential pathway for the transport of sperms from the testes to the outside in a male frog.
options: Testes $\rightarrow$ Vasa efferentia $\rightarrow$ Kidney $\rightarrow$ Bidder's canal $\rightarrow$ Urinogenital duct $\rightarrow$ Cloaca
Testes $\rightarrow$ Vasa efferentia $\rightarrow$ Bidder's canal $\rightarrow$ Kidney $\rightarrow$ Urinogenital duct $\rightarrow$ Cloaca
Testes $\rightarrow$ Vasa efferentia $\rightarrow$ Kidney $\rightarrow$ Urinogenital duct $\rightarrow$ Bidder's canal $\rightarrow$ Cloaca
Testes $\rightarrow$ Bidder's canal $\rightarrow$ Vasa efferentia $\rightarrow$ Kidney $\rightarrow$ Urinogenital duct $\rightarrow$ Cloaca
questions.solution:
In male frogs, sperms are produced in the testes. From the testes, 10 to 12 vasa efferentia arise and enter the kidneys on their respective sides.

Inside the kidneys, they open into the Bidder's canal. The Bidder's canal finally communicates with the urinogenital duct that emerges from the kidneys and opens into the cloaca.

The cloaca is a small, median chamber that is used to pass faecal matter, urine, and sperms to the exterior.

Thus, the correct sequential pathway is: Testes $\rightarrow$ Vasa efferentia $\rightarrow$ Kidney $\rightarrow$ Bidder's canal $\rightarrow$ Urinogenital duct $\rightarrow$ Cloaca.

Answer: Testes $\rightarrow$ Vasa efferentia $\rightarrow$ Kidney $\rightarrow$ Bidder's canal $\rightarrow$ Urinogenital duct $\rightarrow$ Cloaca

It is flanked anteriorly by a large sac-like structure used for storing food, and posteriorly by a ring of 6-8 blind tubules that secrete digestive juice.

Identify the structure described.
questions.solution:
In the alimentary canal of a cockroach, the large sac-like structure used for storing food is the crop. The ring of 6-8 blind tubules that secrete digestive juice is the hepatic or gastric caeca, which is present at the junction of the foregut and midgut.

The structure located immediately between the crop and the hepatic caeca is the gizzard (proventriculus), which helps in grinding the food particles.

Mesenteron (midgut) is posterior to the hepatic caeca. Oesophagus is anterior to the crop. Malpighian tubules are present at the junction of the midgut and hindgut.

Answer: Gizzard

questions.q:
Read the following statement and choose the option that correctly fills the blanks.

In a cockroach, nitrogenous waste is absorbed from the haemolymph by __(A)__, which are lined by __(B)__ cells. The waste is converted into __(C)__ and excreted out through the __(D)__.
options: (A) Hepatic caeca, (B) glandular and ciliated, (C) uric acid, (D) midgut
(A) Malpighian tubules, (B) squamous and cuboidal, (C) urea, (D) hindgut
(A) Malpighian tubules, (B) glandular and ciliated, (C) ammonia, (D) midgut
(A) Malpighian tubules, (B) glandular and ciliated, (C) uric acid, (D) hindgut
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, in a cockroach, excretion is performed by Malpighian tubules (A). Each tubule is lined by glandular and ciliated cells (B). They absorb nitrogenous waste products from the haemolymph and convert them into uric acid (C), which is then excreted out through the hindgut (D).

Hepatic caeca are digestive structures, not excretory. The cellular lining of Malpighian tubules is glandular and ciliated, not squamous or cuboidal. The waste is uric acid, not urea or ammonia, and it exits via the hindgut, not the midgut.

Answer: (A) Malpighian tubules, (B) glandular and ciliated, (C) uric acid, (D) hindgut

questions.solution:

Assertion (A): The moist surface of the buccal cavity and the pharynx are lined by compound epithelium.

Reason (R): Compound epithelium plays a major role in secretion and absorption of substances.

Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true

questions.solution:

Reason (R) is false because compound epithelium, being multi-layered, has a limited role in secretion and absorption. Its primary function is to provide protection against chemical and mechanical stresses. Tissues that play a major role in secretion and absorption are typically simple epithelia, such as simple columnar or simple cuboidal epithelium.

Answer: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false

questions.solution: The colourless blood or haemolymph of cockroach has a clear plasma and numerous white corpuscles called haemocytes. Being devoid of any respiratory pigment, it does not serve for gaseous exchange. Its plasma contains about $70 \%$ water. Rest of it is composed of amino acids, uric acid, proteins, sugars, fats, and salts of sodium, potassium, calcium and magnesium. Transportation of these materials between different parts of body is the main function of haemolymph. In all terrestrial insects, like cockroach, every tissue of body is in direct contact with atmospheric air for gaseous exchange. A complicated system of numerous shiny, transparent and branched air tubes or tracheae is found for this purpose in the haemocoel cavity. Atmospheric air enters into and escapes out from this system through ten pairs of slit-like apertures called stigmata or spiracles, located on lateral sides of body.

questions.q:
Assertion : A mutual exchange of sperms occurs between two earthworms during mating. 
Reason : Mature sperms and egg cells and nutritive fluid are deposited in cocoons produced by gland cells of clitellum.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false
questions.solution:
The earthworms are bisexual or hermaphrodite or monoecious and protandrous. The self-fertilization is not possible in the earthworm because of the relative position of openings of male and female reproductive organs, hence cross fertilization takes place.
During mating, two worms attach themselves with their ventral surfaces and become opposed to each other in opposite direction to exchange packets of sperms called spermatophores. Mature sperm and egg cells and nutritive fluid are deposited in cocoons, produced by the gland cells of clitellum. The ova (eggs) are  fertilized by the sperm cells within the cocoon which then slips off the worm and is deposited in or on the soil. The cocoon holds the worm embryos. After about 3 weeks, each cocoon produces two to twenty baby worms with an average of four.

questions.q: Which of the following is correct regarding respiration in adult frog?
questions.solution: In frog three types of respiration occurs to suit its amphibious mode of life. These are cutaneous, buccopharyngeal and pulmonary respiration. Cutaneous respiration occurs through the thin, moist, highly vascular and naked skin. It takes place in water as well as on land. Buccopharyngeal respiration occurs on land via thin, vascular, moist lining of buccopharyngeal cavity. Pulmonary respiration takes place when the frog is outside the water. It occurs by lungs of adult frog.

options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion

questions.solution:
The blood of cockroach, also called as haemolymph is a mobile connective tissue composed of corpuscles and a colourless fluid, the plasma. It does not contain any respiratory pigment and therefore plays no role in respiration.
Respiratory organs of cockroach are spiracles, tracheae and tracheoles. The respiratory system consists of a network of trachea, that open through 10 pairs of small holes called spiracles present on the lateral side of the body. Thin branching tubes carry oxygen from the air to all the parts. The opening of the spiracles is regulated by the sphincters. Exchange of gases take place at the tracheoles by diffusion.

questions.solution:
Pharyngeal nephridia occur in three pairs of bunches in the 4 th, 5 th and 6 th segments lying on each side of the alimentary canal. The ducts of the nephridia of the sixth segment open into the buccal cavity while the ducts from the nephridia bunches of the fourth and fifth segments open into the pharynx. These ducts carry excretory products from the pharyngeal nephridia into the gut. Enteronephric condition is an adaptation for the conservation of water which is absorbed by the inner lining of the alimentary canal.
Ectonephric nephridia discharge their contents directly to the outside which help the earthworm in keeping the skin moist for cutaneous respiration only. Integumentary nephridia are ectonephric nephridia while, pharyngeal and septal nephridia are enteronephric.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In cockroach, larval and nymphal characters are maintained by
questions.solution: Juvenile hormone is produced by corpora allata in insects, it favours the development of juvenile characteristics. During larval life, this hormone predominates and each moult yields another larger juvenile and keeps the larva in immature condition or maintains juvenility.Ecdysone is a steroidal, moulting hormone of the prothoracic glands, named "ecdysone" in insects that triggers metamorphosis.Salivary glands are the merocrine or epicrine type of gland. Their secretion diffuses out through the cell surface, causing no damage to the cell. In man, 3 pairs of salivary glands are present and in rabbit, they are 4 pairs. Salivary glands are absent in frog.Parotid glands are compound tubulo-acinar glands and are the type of salivary glands with a flask-like secretory portion. Poison gland of a toad is modified parotid gland. In rabbit, parotid glands are the largest salivary gland, present beneath the ears. Duct of parotid gland is known as Stenson's duct in man.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In frog heart, there are cardiac muscles which consists of fibres called
questions.solution:
The heart wall of frog composed of epicardium, myocardium and endocardium. The myocardium is composed of branched and striated yet involuntary cardiac muscles which contracts and relax rhythmically at a fixed rate. The fibres of the self excitatory and conducting muscle of the heart are of three types-nodal fibres, transitional fibres and Purkinje fibres.
In frog heart, a number of muscular ridges called columnae carnae projected from the wall of ventricle into its cavity, dividing the peripheral part of the cavity into a number of pockets.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In frog chromosome number is reduced to half
questions.solution: Each primary oocyte undergo two maturation divisions, first meiotic and the second meiotic division. In the I-meiotic division, the primary oocyte divides into two unequal haploid daughter cells-a large secondary oocyte and very small first polar body. In II-maturation division, the first polar body may divide to form two second polar bodies. The secondary oocyte again divides into two unequal daughter cells, a large ootid and a very small second polar body. The ootid grows into a functional haploid ovum. The I meiotic division is reductional and II meiotic division is equational division.

questions.q: Third cleavage of frog's development is
questions.solution: First and second cleavage in frog are holoblastic, complete, equal, vertical, whereas third cleavage is holoblastic, complete, unequal, latitudinal or horizontal and near the animal pole. It results in the formation 8 cells of which three are black micromeres which have less or no yolk, so divide faster and 4 are colourless macromeres.

questions.q: RBC's are nucleated in
questions.solution: RBC in man is anucleated. Nucleated RBCs are found in camel and amphibians (e.g. frog). In frog, RBCs are typically flattened and more or less eliptical in shape but it appears biconvex when seen along its edge. They are filled with cytoplasm of faint straw colour and contains a definite round nucleus in centre.
